items.title: 68163_Tom Whaley oral history interview
items.q: Milton Berle used to come up to the theater every day and sit there and listen to Alan Drew.

ctx.x: That's what we really want to know about, Tom. The people that the people of the world don't know about now, because they're gone. And they don't know that these were the people that basically were before the Billy Eckstein's and the Lou Rawls and the Johnny Mathis and the Sammy Davis's. So you tell me now, who was this guy?

Alan Drew was an M.C. Milton Berle used to come up to the theater every day and sit there and listen to Alan Drew. The quickest repartee man in the world. But he was dirty, he didn't clean his stuff up. Milton Berle was dirty, but he cleaned it up when he went somewhere. Alan Drew was filthy. But he could -- somebody heckle him, he'd --
Today we got a guy, what's this guy today that we think is filthy but he's making a big name for himself? You know who I'm talking about?
